nodes.title: about AUTO-SAVE
widgets_values:
**AUTO-SAVE (this box)**

Keeps a copy of **every** picture in `comfyui/output/freedom_archive/` the moment it's made - your 'never lose anything' pile.

STEP 9's pick box runs at the same time, no conflict - use it to send only the keepers to your own folder. Delete this box if you don't want the archive.

nodes.title: STEP 9 - see it & save it
widgets_values:
**STEP 9 - see it, pick it, save it**

Every picture is already archived automatically by the AUTO-SAVE box, off to the right, so nothing is ever lost. This step is where you send the keepers to a folder of your own. After Run, your picture(s) show here with tick boxes.

- One picture -> **Save Image**.
- A batch -> tick the ones you want -> **Save Selected Images**.

**Set User Save Folder** (button under Save Image) opens a Windows folder window. Your choice is stored in this workflow, so it sticks when you save the workflow. **Open Folder** shows it in Explorer.

nodes.title: STEP 7 - the actual painting
widgets_values:
**STEP 7 - the actual painting**

This is where the picture gets made. It takes the painter (STEP 1), your want / don't-want (STEPS 4-5) and the blank canvas (STEP 6), and cleans up random noise into an image over **26 passes**.

- **seed** = the random starting point. Same seed + same words = same picture.
- **control_after_generate**: `randomize` = new picture each Run; `fixed` = keep tweaking the same one.
- Leave steps / cfg / sampler as they are - they're tuned for bigLust.

nodes.title: READ ME FIRST
widgets_values:
## How to make a picture

1. In the **green box (STEP 4)** type what you want to see. Plain sentences are fine.
2. Press the blue **Run** button, top right.
3. Wait 15-60 seconds. The picture(s) show up in **STEP 9**.

Every picture is archived automatically to `comfyui/output/freedom_archive/`, so
nothing you make is ever lost. STEP 9 is where you send the *keepers* somewhere of
your own: click **Save Image** for a single picture, or tick the ones you want and
click **Save Selected Images**. **Set User Save Folder**, the button under Save
Image, chooses where those copies go.

That's it. Everything else is already set up.

### If you want to change something
- **Different look / model:** click the file name in STEP 1.
- **Her face on or off:** the **FACE ON / FACE OFF** button on STEP 2. Switched off,
  the same picture is painted with a generic person instead, and the card you picked
  is remembered for when you switch back.
- **Add-on LoRAs:** STEP 3 starts with three rows and grows to twelve with
  **+ Add LoRA**. Tick a row on, pick from the dropdown, set how strong it is - it
  only lists LoRAs that actually match this checkpoint, so nothing you pick can be
  the wrong architecture. (Emotions, expression\_helper and Hands zib are NOT SDXL -
  they are Flux / Krea / Z-Image LoRAs and will not appear here or work with
  bigLust or Pony. This note used to say otherwise; that was wrong.)
- **Wider or taller:** change the numbers in STEP 6.
- **New random picture, same idea:** just press Run again.
- **Keep the same picture, tweak wording:** on **STEP 7** set *control_after_generate*
  to `fixed`, change a few words, Run.

nodes.title: STEP 1 - the art model
widgets_values:
**STEP 1 - the art model**

This opens the 'brain' that knows how to paint - **bigLust**, a photo-real model made for adult images.

It feeds three things to the rest of the recipe: the painter, the part that reads your words, and the part that turns the result into a normal picture.

**You touch this only** to switch models - click the file name to pick lustify, CyberRealistic Pony, etc.

nodes.title: STEP 4 - what you want
widgets_values:
**STEP 4 - what you want**

**This is the main box - type here.**

Describe the picture in plain sentences: who, where, the lighting, the mood. Example: *a red-haired woman by a rainy window, soft light, sharp photo*.

More detail = closer to what you pictured.

**If you picked someone on STEP 2's Face Shelf**, her trigger word is glued onto the front of whatever you type here automatically - you don't need to type it yourself. The two small boxes below this one just do that gluing; you never need to touch them.

nodes.title: STEP 3 - add other LoRAs
widgets_values:
**STEP 3 - add other LoRAs**

A LoRA is a small add-on file that teaches the art model one specific thing - a clothing item, a pose, a style - on top of what it already knows. This is different from STEP 2: STEP 2 is for a trained *person's face*; this step is for everything else.

Three rows are ready to go. Tick a row on, pick a LoRA from its dropdown, and set its **strength** (0.8 is a safe starting point - higher can overpower the picture). Click **+ Add LoRA** for more rows, or the **X** on a row to remove it.

You will not see any of her trained faces in this list - those only live in STEP 2, so you can't load the wrong one here by mistake.

nodes.title: STEP 2 - pick her face
widgets_values:
**STEP 2 - pick her face**

This is the shelf of every face you've trained. Click a picture to put that person's face - or face and body - onto whatever gets painted below. Each trained person shows up as two cards: one for face-only, one for face + body.

**The FACE ON / FACE OFF switch.** At the top of the shelf is a button that reads **FACE ON** in green. It decides whether this whole step does anything at all. Click it once and it turns red and reads **FACE OFF**.

**What FACE OFF really means.** The picture gets painted exactly as if this step were not in the workflow at all. Her face is not applied, and her trigger word is left out of your prompt as well. (A trigger word is the made-up word her training gave her, something like `br1tany woman`. It is the word that tells the art model to draw her and not a stranger.) So with the switch off, nothing about her reaches the picture - not her face, and not her name.

**Your pick is not lost.** The card you clicked stays clicked, just greyed out, and switching back on brings her straight back at the same strength. That is the difference between this switch and the **None** button beside it: **None** forgets who you picked, while the switch only pauses her.

**Two buttons, one switch.** You can flip it from the button on the shelf, or from the small toggle on the node itself just above the shelf, which reads **face ON** / **face OFF**. They are wired together, so moving either one moves both. You never have to wonder which one is in charge.

**When to use it.** Turn her off to try a new prompt, a new pose, or a different art model on a generic person first, so her face isn't pulling the picture around while you experiment. Then turn her back on and make the real one.

The **strength** slider controls how strongly her face takes over - 0.9 is a good starting point. Lower it toward 0.7 if her face comes out stiff, raise it toward 1.0 if it doesn't look enough like her.

**Refresh** picks up any face you've just finished training without restarting anything.
